concerns.text: SC-004 requires the *full* end‑to‑end pipeline (all scenarios × all latency steps) to complete within 6 h on a CPU‑only runner, but the only runtime check is T013 which runs on a *sample* of 5 scenarios and asserts < 30 min. No task measures the full‑dataset runtime, so the success criterion is not verified and the claim is effectively weakened.

FR-009 mandates the calculation of behavioral metrics (Task Completion Rate, Semantic Coherence, Interruption Count) that are independent of the injected delay. No task in the list implements or validates these metrics, leaving the functional requirement uncovered.

FR-006 states the pipeline must run without model quantization or GPU/CUDA acceleration. The task list contains no explicit verification step (e.g., a test that asserts `torch.cuda.is_available()` is false or that no GPU‑specific libraries are imported), so the requirement is not enforced.

SC-001 requires *all* target EVA‑Bench scenarios to be latency‑perturbed without corruption. The verification for T006 only checks a *single* chosen scenario (inter‑turn silence 200 ms ± 10 ms and checksum match). This does not guarantee that every scenario meets the same integrity constraints, thus the acceptance criterion is weakened.

FR-007 claims pipeline optimization to finish within 6 h, yet there is no dedicated measurement or profiling task (e.g., a benchmark that records total wall‑clock time for the full dataset). The claim remains untested, constituting a silent weakening of the functional requirement.
